horse.prompt:
Use case: historical-scene. Create one photorealistic widescreen 16:9 film reference frame for an ancient Chinese war drama, late Eastern Han / Three Kingdoms, Yiling, summer night AD 222. Single full-bleed frame, absolutely no text or panels.
FIRST PERSON from a rider galloping on a dark bay horse on a narrow dirt track along low mountains toward a distant military encampment. Frame is mostly the horse's powerful moving neck, mane and two natural ears in the lower half, camera just above the neck looking forward. One pair of simple worn leather reins leads out below frame; no rider face or torso, no other people. Four-legged anatomically correct horse, believable bridle, no ornament.
Deep moonless blue-black night. Beyond layered dark mountain silhouettes the low clouds and hanging smoke at the distant camp are starting to glow dull dark crimson-orange from a large fire hidden partly behind the ridge. This is firelight reflected on smoke, NOT sunrise, NOT sunset, NOT a red sun, NOT supernatural red sky. Only a few distant flame points visible near mountain foot, not a huge wall of fire immediately in the horse's path. Restrained project look: ink-dark hills, warm fire glow with a physical source, natural brown hide, low saturated night atmosphere, real cloth and leather. Motion implied by wind-whipped mane and slight peripheral motion blur; horse neck and ears remain sharp enough as identity reference. Ground uneven and dry with some loose dust, no modern roads, no buildings, no flaming horse, no weapons foreground. Cinematic actual live-action realism.
horse.visualReview: 骑手视角、马颈与耳、远山红烟、夜间火源已查看。

pangtong.prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve historical-scene. Create ONE photorealistic 16:9 horizontal single-shot film composition reference, no panels, no captions.
Reference image 1 is the established Pang Tong six-view character reference: lock the exact same mature East Asian man's face, narrow long face, high forehead, knitted brows, thin moustache and pointed goatee, tall dark ribbed cloth crown, deep indigo patterned cross-collar robe with reddish-brown thin piping and beige-gray inner collar. Reference image 2 is the prop reference sheet: use ONLY the large three-quarter bronze seal at left for geometry and materials. Do NOT reproduce any reference sheet layout or clay impression.
We are looking from the player's eye height directly at Pang Tong in an earlier dream. He is a physically solid human, not a transparent ghost. Frontal medium shot crown to waist, 1.2m away, eyes directed gently toward the camera, mouth naturally closed awaiting dialogue, serious restrained expression. Dark indeterminate room or dream space, smooth near-black background, no visible modern furnishings and no thick fog or fantasy effects. Soft warm practical-looking side illumination from viewer left catches his cheek, fingers and dark blue robe, subtle cool fill gives cloth shape, a narrow suggestion of amber light behind far left without showing a candle prop.
Pang Tong holds out his RIGHT hand palm up toward the viewer at lower center-left of frame, elbow still bent and hand just forward of waist, not a thrusting action. Resting flat on his right palm is the SAME SMALL approximately 2.2cm bronze seal: square brown bronze body, low arched perforated knob, short faded reddish-brown cord, a small chipped corner. The physical bronze side and knob are visible, inscription underside hidden by his palm. The tiny seal must fit comfortably in the palm, NOT huge. His other hand rests naturally near the belt. Do not include the player's receiving hand yet. All five fingers anatomically correct and not fused with the seal or cord. Need crown, recognizable face, torso and prop-bearing palm all clearly within frame. Film realism matching user reference, natural pores and cloth. No halo, glowing eyes, magical effects, background fire, subtitles, readable writing, grids or watermarks.
pangtong.framingRevision: Edit this exact reference frame, preserving the same man, face identity, expression, dark indigo patterned robe, right hand palm-up bearing the same tiny bronze seal with reddish cord, left hand near belt, lighting and dark background. Correct framing ONLY: move the virtual camera back approximately 15 percent so the entire tall crown is visible with a clear margin of dark background above it (at least 8 percent of frame height), and both his seal-bearing palm and belt remain fully within the frame. Keep horizontal 16:9, eye-level frontal medium shot. The crown has the same complete ribbed crisscross construction as visible, reconstruct its small missing top naturally. Do not change his age, beard, facial proportions, seal size, gesture or lighting. No text, no borders, no inset, no other people or objects.
